description: Independently justified proof obligations for change-scoped selection. Each fixture records what a change MUST prove for reasons established OUTSIDE the selector - a real fix and the test that shipped with it, a declared impact contract, or a policy decision - never a recording of what some earlier version of the selector happened to choose. Freezing a selector's own output as its oracle would prove only that the mechanism still agrees with itself.
contract: The selector may become narrower or smarter over time. It may NEVER omit an obligation listed here.

fixtures.provenance: commit 5d48920f0 fix(raft): boundary-aware prefix revalidation in follower batch tail
fixtures.why: a consensus log-tail fix; storage-raft is the semantic home and its proof must run

fixtures.provenance: commit 555e4b4f5 fix(schema-admission): drain-aware grace deadline for quiescence gate
fixtures.why: the two tests shipped WITH this fix, so they are independently known to be the witnesses for it; the change spans two owners, so both subsystems are obligations

fixtures.provenance: impact-contracts.json contract 'wit-world-interface' declares wit/ owners with wasm-service witnesses
fixtures.why: the registry independently declares that every WASM consumer depends on this interface
routing envelope changes are declared cross-boundary in the registry

fixtures.provenance: bootstrap-contract in impact-contracts.json; join is the highest-coupling lifecycle path
fixtures.why: node join affects membership, and the bootstrap contract declares its consumers

fixtures.provenance: policy: the selector cannot be trusted to scope proof of its own change
fixtures.why: a change to selection must prove the selection machinery; these also sit in the unconditional spine, so this fixture additionally pins the bootstrap
the case the old gate paid 2065 tests for

fixtures.provenance: policy: fail closed on unclassifiable change
fixtures.why: silent under-selection is indistinguishable from correct selection

fixtures.provenance: policy: the installed dependency graph is broader than any subsystem
fixtures.why: proven the hard way on 2026-08-18: an undeclared dependency made the committed import graph unreproducible on any clean checkout

fixtures.provenance: policy: exports/bin/files define what consumers install and execute
fixtures.why: no subsystem proof covers the published package surface

fixtures.provenance: policy: developer command wiring is not the runtime surface. The obligation is that a scripts edit stays MODULAR; it originally recorded release-packaging because that was the modular answer at the time, which is the corpus recording a mechanism output rather than its obligation.
fixtures.why: scripts edits must stay modular, or every command tweak forces a release proof. They prove the development loop, not the packaging surface: routing them to release-packaging dragged the npm distribution proof into ordinary CI.

fixtures.provenance: impact-contracts.json coupledPairs 'priority-services-row-publication-census'; the registry independently declares these two owners must stay consistent
fixtures.why: changing the row-publication endpoint must also prove the census endpoint's subsystem, exactly one hop and no further
the opposite endpoint lives in src/workflow, a different subsystem, so this fixture proves cross-subsystem coupling rather than same-subsystem coupling
